League+]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]]. ==High school career== Graham played high school basketball at [[St. Mary's Ryken High School]] in [[Leonardtown, Maryland]] for Head Coach Dave Tallman, where as a senior he was named to the ''[[Washington Post]]'' All-Met team for the [[Washington D.C.]] area after averaging 21.5 points and 12 rebounds per game.{{cite news | title = 2010-11 Winter All-Met | newspaper = [[Washington Post]] | date = April 8, 2011| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/sports/highschools/2010-2011-winter-all-met/boys-basketball/ | access-date = November 14, 2013}} Graham chose to play for coach [[Shaka Smart]] at [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] after also considering [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]] and [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]].{{cite web | title = Treveon Graham VCU athletic bio | work = [[VCU Rams]] | url = http://www.vcuathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2013-14/bios/graham_treveon_9tnq | access-date = November 14, 2013 | archive-date = October 28, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131028045818/http://www.vcuathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2013-14/bios/graham_treveon_9tnq | url-status = dead }} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]], Graham became a part of the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|Rams]]' regular rotation and averaged 7.0 [[Points per game|points]] and 3.2 [[rebounds per game]]. Prior to the start of his sophomore season, he was chosen by [[Sports Illustrated]] as the most likely "breakout sophomore" in the nation, based on statistical analysis of his performance in limited minutes as a freshman.{{cite magazine | last = Winn | first = Luke | title = Treveon Graham, Andre Hollins to make impact in sophomore season | magazine = [[Sports Illustrated]] | date = September 5, 2012 | url = http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/luke_winn/09/04/NCAA-basketball-sophomore-breakout/ | archive-url = https://archive.today/20131115022828/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/luke_winn/09/04/NCAA-basketball-sophomore-breakout/ | url-status = dead | archive-date = November 15, 2013 | access-date = November 14, 2013}} Graham's performance did improve significantly in his second season, raising his averages to 15.1 points and 5.8 rebounds as a full-time starter. His performance was good enough to earn him second team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] honors.{{cite web | title = Wyatt, Crews, Weber, Christon Claim Top Men's Basketball Honors | work = [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] | date = March 12, 2013 | url = http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=799991&SPID=136228&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=208923429 | access-date = November 14, 2013}} [[File:Treveon Graham free throw.jpg|thumb|Graham with the VCU Rams in 2013]] After his sophomore season, Graham was chosen for [[United States men's national basketball team|USA Basketball]]'s entry to the [[2013 Summer Universiade]] in [[Kazan]], Russia. He started 5 games for Team USA, averaging 9.4 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web | title = Twenty-Seventh World University Games -- 2013 | work = [[USA Basketball]] | url = http://www.usab.com/history/world-university-games-mens/twenty-seventh-world-university-games-2013.aspx | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150629001611/http://www.usab.com/history/world-university-games-mens/twenty-seventh-world-university-games-2013.aspx | url-status = dead | archive-date = June 29, 2015 | access-date = November 14, 2013}} Prior to the 2013–14 season, Graham was named first team preseason All-Atlantic 10 as VCU was named the preseason favorite to win the league.{{cite web | title = VCU Picked to Win A-10 Men's Basketball; 21 Players Earn Preseason Honors | work = [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] | date = October 8, 2013 | url = http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=799991&SPID=136228&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=209278456 | access-date = November 14, 2013}} VCU entered the season ranked 14th in the preseason [[AP Poll]]. The Rams scored a key early season road victory, beating 25th ranked [[2013–14 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] on November 12 in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]]. Graham led all scorers with 22 points, including the game-winning [[Three-point field goal|three-pointer]] with just over a second remaining.{{cite web | last = Johnson| first = Raphielle| title = Treveon Graham's three-pointer the difference as VCU beats Virginia (VIDEO) | work = [[NBCSports.com]] | date = November 12, 2013| url = http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/11/12/treveon-grahams-three-pointer-the-difference-as-vcu-beats-virginia-video/ | access-date = November 14, 2013}} As a senior in 2014–15, Graham averaged 16.2 points and 7.1 rebounds in 33 games.{{cite web | title = Treveon Graham Stats | work = Sports-reference.com | url = https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/treveon-graham-1.html | access-date = August 17, 2015}} Despite being affected by a lingering ankle injury for large parts of the season, Graham helped VCU in many ways. He led VCU in scoring, rebounding, and three-pointers made. He was also their leading scorer during the A-10 tournament where VCU won their first conference tournament in the Atlantic 10 despite qualifying as the fifth seed. During Graham's college career he averaged 13.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 25.4 minutes per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/grahatr01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Treveon Graham Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=December 3, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Idaho Stampede (2015–2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Graham joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web | title = Spurs Announce 2015 Summer League Rosters for Utah & Las Vegas | work = NBA.com | date = July 3, 2015| url = http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2015-summer-league-rosters-utah-las-vegas | access-date = August 17, 2015}} On August 17, 2015, he signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web | title = Jazz Sign Free Agent Treveon Graham | work = NBA.com | date = August 17, 2015| url = http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-free-agent-treveon-graham | access-date = August 17, 2015}} However, he was later waived by the Jazz on October 20 after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-bryce-cotton-and-treveon-graham|title=Jazz Waive Bryce Cotton and Treveon Graham|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2015|access-date=October 20, 2015}} On November 1, he was acquired by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Jazz.{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065740|title=Idaho Stampede Finalize 2015 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 1, 2015|access-date=November 1, 2015}} In 46 games for the Stampede in 2015–16, he averaged 15.7 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/g/grahatr01d.html|title=Treveon Graham D-League Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 7, 2016}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2016–2018)=== In July 2016, Graham joined the [[Orlando Magic]] white team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|Orlando Summer League]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-announce-2016-southwest-airlines-orlando-pro-summer-league-roster/|title=Magic Announce 2016 Southwest Airlines Orlando Pro Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2016|access-date=July 26, 2016}} and the Utah Jazz for the Las Vegas Summer League. On July 26, 2016, he signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-guard/forward-treveon-graham|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Guard/Forward Treveon Graham|work=NBA.com|date=July 26, 2016|access-date=July 26, 2016}} In his second game for the Hornets on November 7, 2016, Graham scored his first NBA points when he knocked down a three-pointer from the left wing during a 122–100 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899545|title=Hornets roll over Pacers 122-100 behind strong first half|work=ESPN.com|date=November 7, 2016|access-date=November 7, 2016}} On April 10, 2017, he scored a career-high 14 points in an 89–79 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900585|title=Bucks brush past Hornets for 89-79 win|work=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2017|access-date=April 10, 2017}} On June 29, 2018, the Hornets announced that they would decline a qualifying offer to Graham, making him a free agent.{{cite news|title=Hornets Decline Qualifying Offers To Treveon Graham, Marcus Paige|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-decline-qualifying-offers-treveon-graham-marcus-paige|access-date=June 29, 2018|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=June 29, 2018}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019)=== On July 30, 2018, Graham signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Treveon Graham |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/30/brooklyn-nets-sign-treveon-graham |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 28, 2018 |date=July 30, 2018}} On the season, Graham appeared in 35 games, scoring 5.3 points per game. During the season, he was sidelined for two months with a hamstring injury. Graham did a rehab stint with the [[Long Island Nets]] before returning to Brooklyn.{{cite news|title=Shannon Scott records 20 assists and Treveon Graham returns to action in Long Island win|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/platform/amp/2019/1/3/18166450/shannon-scott-records-20-assists-and-treveon-graham-returns-to-action-in-long-island-win|access-date=July 24, 2019|work=[[SBNation.com]]|date=January 3, 2019}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2020)=== On July 7, 2019, Graham was sent to the [[Golden State Warriors]] as part of a trade package for [[Kevin Durant]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-russell-20190707|title=Warriors Acquire All-Star Guard D'Angelo Russell From Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2019}} The following day, Graham and [[Shabazz Napier]] were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Lior Eliyahu]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-shabazz-napier-and-treveon-graham|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Shabazz Napier and Treveon Graham|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2019}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2020)=== On January 16, 2020, Graham, along with [[Jeff Teague (basketball)|Jeff Teague]], was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Allen Crabbe]].{{cite web |title=Hawks Acquire Jeff Teague And Treveon Graham From Minnesota In Exchange For Allen Crabbe |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-teague-graham-in-exchange-for-crabbe |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 16, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}} ===Long Island Nets (2022–2023)=== On January 25, 2022, Graham was acquired off waivers by the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=January 25, 2022}} ===Montreal Alliance (2023)=== On May 2, 2023, Graham signed with the [[Montreal Alliance]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=NBA Veteran Treveon Graham Signs With Alliance For 2023 Season|url=https://www.cebl.ca/nba-veteran-treveon-graham-signs-with-alliance-for-2023-season|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 2, 2023|access-date=May 5, 2023}} With Montreal, Graham averaged 14.6 points and 9.3 rebounds per game. He finished second in the CEBL in rebounding behind [[Simi Shittu]] of the [[Calgary Surge]].{{cite web |title=CEBL League Leaders 2023 Season - CEBL Player Stats |url=https://www.cebl.ca/league-leaders-2023 |website=www.cebl.ca |language=en}} ===Motor City Cruise (2023–2024)=== On October 21, 2023, Graham signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]],{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed Treveon Graham, David Nwaba, Nate Roberts and Ryan Turell to {{as written|Ex|ibit [sic]}} 10 contracts.|number=1715746303668289656|user=Pistons_PR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} but was waived the same day.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Pistons Sign, Waive David Nwaba, Three Others|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/pistons-sign-waive-david-nwaba-three-others.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} Nine days later, he joined the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite tweet|author=Motor City Cruise|title=The engine is revving, and we're ready to roll! Check out the Motor City Cruise training camp roster - we're ready to work! #HustleAndDrive|number=1719088094782132699|user=MotorCityCruise|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} However, he was waived on January 26, 2024.{{cite tweet|author=Motor City Cruise|title=Thank you for your contributions to the Motor City, @TreBall21! OFFICIAL - We have waived Treveon Graham from his contract.|number=1750996731683070338|user=MotorCityCruise|date=January 26, 2024|access-date=January 27, 2024}} ===Taoyuan Pauian Pilots (2024–present)=== On February 7, 2024, Graham signed with the [[Taoyuan Pauian Pilots]] of the [[P. League+]].{{cite web|title=NBA資歷新洋將加入 領航猿目標季後賽|url=https://udn.com/news/story/7002/7761093|website=UDN.com|date=February 7, 2024|access-date=February 7, 2024|language=Chinese}} On July 31, he re-signed with the Taoyuan Pauian Pilots.{{cite web |title=領航猿續約第六人伯朗、暖男葛拉漢 兩人季後賽關鍵表現獲肯定 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2788284 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=February 19, 2025 |date=July 31,
